title: MLOps Patterns
summary: The vocabulary of taking machine learning to production — the ML lifecycle, data versioning, feature stores, experiment tracking, model registries, distributed training, model serving, drift monitoring, A/B testing for ML, CI/CD for ML, platform choice (build vs buy), and the LLMOps surface in 2026.

volatileChapters.reason: LLMOps is the fastest-moving subdiscipline; new tools (LangSmith, LangFuse, Arize Phoenix) and patterns (RAG, agent ops, fine-tuning) shift quarterly.

inspiredBy.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems (Chip Huyen) + Machine Learning Engineering (Andriy Burkov) + Google MLOps guides

chapters.title: Why MLOps
chapters.summary: The ML production gap — how production differs from research notebooks, the 87% never-deployed statistic, Sculley's hidden technical debt paper, and what MLOps inherits from DevOps and SRE.

chapters.title: The ML Lifecycle
chapters.summary: Data → train → evaluate → deploy → monitor → retrain — the full loop, where it differs from software lifecycles (data is code, models can decay), and the maturity-level framing (Google MLOps Levels 0/1/2).

chapters.title: Data Versioning
chapters.summary: Reproducibility for data — DVC, Pachyderm, Delta Lake, LakeFS, Git LFS; immutable data snapshots, hash-based pinning, the reproducibility-vs-storage tradeoff, lineage tracking.

chapters.title: Feature Stores
chapters.summary: The training/serving parity problem — online vs offline feature stores, Feast, Tecton, point-in-time correctness, feature serving SLAs, the build-vs-buy decision.

chapters.title: Experiment Tracking
chapters.summary: Runs, artifacts, lineage — MLflow, Weights & Biases, Neptune, Comet; tracking hyperparameters, metrics, models, code; the reproducibility minimum.

chapters.title: Model Registry
chapters.summary: Versioned model storage — lifecycle stages (staging/production/archived), approval workflows, model cards, the registry as system-of-record for deployed models.

chapters.title: Training Infrastructure
chapters.summary: Distributed training — data parallel vs model parallel, parameter servers, allreduce, Kubeflow, SageMaker, Vertex AI Training, the GPU/TPU economics, spot training.

chapters.title: Model Serving
chapters.summary: Online vs batch vs streaming — REST/gRPC endpoints, batch inference, streaming inference, the latency/throughput tradeoffs, KServe, BentoML, Triton, TorchServe, model server choices.

chapters.title: Model Monitoring
chapters.summary: Drift detection — input drift, concept drift, prediction drift, label drift; performance decay, shadow models, the ground-truth-arrives-late problem, monitoring without labels.

chapters.title: A/B Testing for ML
chapters.summary: Online evaluation — interleaving, shadow traffic, gradual rollout, multi-armed bandits, the offline-vs-online metric gap, the counterfactual problem, real significance vs lift hunting.

chapters.title: CI/CD for ML
chapters.summary: Testing models in CI — data validation tests, model behavior tests, fairness tests, the training-serving skew problem, automated retraining triggers, model deployment patterns.

chapters.title: ML Platforms
chapters.summary: Build vs buy — in-house platforms (Uber Michelangelo, Airbnb Bighead, Netflix Metaflow) vs SaaS (Databricks, SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure ML); the platform-engineering for ML pattern.

chapters.title: LLMOps in 2026
chapters.summary: The new ML ops surface — RAG operations, prompt versioning, eval pipelines, fine-tuning operations, agent observability, cost telemetry, the LLMOps vs MLOps distinction.
